profile.name: Somanadh K
profile.headline: I build systems that think.
profile.tagline: Building intelligent systems, one problem at a time.
profile.intro: I'm a Computer Science student and AI engineering intern focused on developing intelligent applications, backend systems, AI agents, and retrieval-augmented generation solutions. I enjoy exploring how AI can solve practical problems and turning ideas into working software.
about: I am a Computer Science and Engineering student who works at the meeting point of language models and the systems around them. My interest is less in the demo and more in the distance between a demo and something a person can actually use: the API behind it, the retrieval that grounds it, the agent loop that has to fail gracefully.

As a Forward Deployed AI Engineer Intern, I worked on AI-powered applications, intelligent workflows, backend integrations, and LLM-driven solutions. Before that, I spent a semester as a Web Development Intern, which is where the product instinct started.

I am early in my career and deliberate about saying so. What I have is curiosity, hands-on internship experience, and a growing body of work in agentic AI, retrieval, and backend engineering. What I do not have is a decade of production war stories, and I would rather show you the real thing.

projects.name: SOMANADH.OS
projects.tagline: A living intelligence portfolio, built as a real system.
projects.summary: This website: a cinematic Next.js portfolio with a grounded AI assistant, a FastAPI backend, privacy-conscious visitor analytics, and a private content studio.
projects.problem: A portfolio usually asks a recruiter to trust a PDF. I wanted a place where the claim and the proof are the same artifact: the assistant answers from verified records, the analytics are real, and the interface is the engineering sample.
projects.whyItMatters: It demonstrates the whole path of an AI feature — prompt design, retrieval, streaming transport, failure fallbacks, rate limits, privacy boundaries — instead of a UI wrapped around an API key.
projects.architecture: Next.js App Router renders content and proxies every browser request to a FastAPI service. The browser only ever talks to first-party routes, so the OpenRouter key never leaves the server. FastAPI owns content, retrieval, analytics ingestion, admin sessions, and uploads; SQLAlchemy talks to SQLite locally and Postgres in production. The admin dashboard reads aggregated SQL, and live presence streams over Server-Sent Events.
projects.implementation: Content is seeded from a single JSON source of truth into content tables and re-read at request time, so the studio updates the site without a deploy. The assistant builds a knowledge base from those records, retrieves by lexical relevance plus intent, and streams answers through an SSE pipeline. Without an OpenRouter key it answers deterministically from the same records instead of pretending to call a model.
challenges: Keeping a visually heavy homepage fast: the neural scene is lazy-loaded, capped at a modest device pixel ratio, paused off-screen, and replaced by a static composition for reduced-motion visitors.
Making the assistant honest: the unverified project records had to produce an explicit 'not published yet', not a plausible invention.
Analytics that respect visitors: anonymous identifiers, consent gating, no raw IP storage, and country data only when the host provides it.
decisions: Server-side proxy instead of exposing the API directly, so credentials and cookies stay off the client.
Structured lexical retrieval instead of pgvector: with a corpus this small, embeddings would add infrastructure without improving grounded answers.
Deterministic fallback answers as a first-class mode, not an error screen.
SSE for streamed answers and live admin pulses: no WebSocket infrastructure for a single-instance dashboard.
lessons: The hard part of an AI feature is the boundary: what the model may say, what happens when it fails, and what the system refuses to do.
Performance is an art-direction problem — the most expensive effect is usually not the one carrying the concept.
future: Deploy the frontend and API, then publish verified screenshots and a walkthrough.
Add a project-level architecture viewer with per-node explanations.
Move rate limiting to Redis if the API runs on more than one instance.
projects.note: Built and tested locally. Deployment configuration is documented in the repository; live URL and repository link will be added once published.

beyond.headline: BEYOND THE CODE
beyond.standfirst: The part of the system that is not a system.
paragraphs: I am drawn to problems that sit awkwardly between disciplines — where the model is only half the answer and the other half is a schema, a permission boundary, or a sentence a user actually understands.

The way I work is simple: read the requirement twice, build the smallest honest version, then make it survive contact with a real person. I would rather ship a narrow feature that holds than a wide one that only demos well.

Leading the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology chapter has sharpened a question I keep returning to: intelligence is not the hard part to justify — consequences are. That shapes how I want to build.

principles.title: Curiosity, operationalised
principles.body: New model, new framework, new failure mode — I learn by rebuilding the thing until the mental model holds.

principles.title: Product before polish
principles.body: A feature earns its animation only after it earns its place in the workflow.

principles.title: Honest engineering
principles.body: No invented metrics. No borrowed seniority. Clear about what works, clearer about what does not yet.

principles.title: Systems thinking
principles.body: Every model call has a cost, a latency budget, and a failure path. Design all three.
